## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Pasūrasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 8) is the eighth treatise of the *Mahāniddesa*, which forms part of the late canonical exegesis of the Khuddaka Nikāya in the Pali Tipiṭaka [SuttaCentral]. Rendered by Bhikkhu Sujato as the "Exposition of the Discourse to Pasūra on Debate", it provides an extensive word-by-word commentary on the *Pasūra Sutta* (Snp 4.8 / PTS Snp 161) of the *Aṭṭhakavagga* [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral records two modern translations of the treatise in two languages [SuttaCentral]. Passages or themes associated with the text are cited or referenced across a wide range of canonical and post-canonical literature, including other Niddesa treatises (Mnd 13, Mnd 14, Mnd 16, Cnd 19), the *Saṃyutta Nikāya* (SN 22.58), the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 3.1), the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37), and the *Milindapañha* (Mil 5.4.10, Mil 5.5.4) [SuttaCentral].

Curated passage-level parallels identified on SuttaCentral connect the text to the *Nandamāṇavapucchāniddesa* (Cnd 11), the *Suddhaṭṭhakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 4), and the Abhidhamma's *Dhammasaṅgaṇi* (Ds 2.1.1) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus detects widespread Pali-internal text reuse amounting to 2,842 matching passages shared across 135 texts [DharmaNexus]. In agreement with SuttaCentral, substantial textual overlap exists with Cnd 11 (§64.3–67.2 ↔ §10.1–11.2) and Ps 3.1 (§78.15_0–83.4 ↔ §23.13–29.4); the largest sharing of formulaic exegetical prose occurs with other *Mahāniddesa* chapters, particularly the *Mahābyūhasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 13), *Tuvaṭakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 14), *Cūḷabyūhasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 12), and *Sāriputtasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 16), as well as the commentary *Mahāniddesa-aṭṭhakathā* [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also automatically aligns segments with external corpora, including the Chinese *Madhyama Āgama* (T 26), Sanskrit philosophical works such as Candrakīrti's *Prasannapadā* and Nāgārjuna's *Dharmasaṃgraha*, and Tibetan translations of Mahāyāna sūtras such as the *Laṅkāvatārasūtra* (D0107) [DharmaNexus].
